## Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena in 8 days: what the itinerary reveals

This tour focuses on Colombia's cities: [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) tells the country's story through museums and civic squares, [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) through urban transformation and Comuna 13, and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) through colonial architecture and the defences of its Caribbean port.

The journey lasts 8 days and 7 nights: 2 nights in Bogotá, 2 in Medellín and 3 in Cartagena. For a first visit, it offers an alternative to longer nature-focused itineraries. Most of the time is devoted to culture and city life, with an excursion to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and a free day by the sea.

## Bogotá: four hours exploring the historic centre

The Bogotá tour takes in La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, Casa de la Moneda, the Botero Museum and Bolívar Square. Together, these sites trace pre-Columbian heritage, colonial architecture and twentieth-century art. The mountains surrounding the capital provide a very different backdrop from the Caribbean coast later in the journey.

Allow approximately 4 hours for the tour. Museum opening days matter when planning: the Gold Museum closes on Mondays, while Casa de la Moneda and the Botero Museum have Tuesday restrictions. These conditions affect the order of visits. Learn more on our [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) destination page.

Excursions to [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) and the [Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) belong to other itinerary options, including the [12-day programme featuring Caño Cristales](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-beyond/). On this tour, the main Bogotá sightseeing excursion stays within the city.

## Medellín: from Pueblito Paisa to Comuna 13

After the flight to Medellín, a separate day is reserved for discovering the city. The driving portion covers Pueblito Paisa, central and administrative districts, public spaces and El Poblado. A walking tour of Comuna 13 with a local guide follows.

Comuna 13 is known for its graffiti, street art, escalators and transformed public spaces. Leaving the vehicle matters here: the neighbourhood's story unfolds on foot, along its stairways and narrow streets. What makes this day memorable is Colombia's modern urban history rather than another colonial square.

The next excursion heads to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). Colourful decorative relief panels known as zócalos distinguish the town's houses. Nearby stands the Piedra del Peñol rock, with views across the reservoir. A mototaxi ride through Guatapé is included, while climbing the staircase of more than 600 steps costs extra. An additional boat trip is also optional.

## Why the day in Guatapé needs careful planning

Day five is packed: travel to Piedra del Peñol and Guatapé, return to Medellín, an airport transfer and a flight to Cartagena. This is a long private excursion of around 11 hours. When choosing a flight, allow for more than driving time: stops, a possible climb up the rock and the transfer across the city all need to be considered.

**The domestic Medellín–Cartagena flight is not included**, nor is the Bogotá–Medellín flight. Their costs and actual schedules need to be factored into the trip arrangements. If you would prefer a leisurely full day at the rock, it makes sense to discuss adjusting the itinerary rather than automatically adding every optional activity to the original programme.

## Cartagena: the fortress, La Popa and a free day

Cartagena's programme includes the hilltop La Popa monastery, San Felipe de Barajas Fortress, the historic centre and the Las Bóvedas artisan district. The city's fortification system is part of a UNESCO World Heritage property. It offers a way to understand the Caribbean coast through the history of its port and defensive structures.

One free day follows the sightseeing tour. You can spend it wandering through the historic centre or choose a trip to the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/). The [San Pedro de Majagua day trip](/colombia/rosario-islands/colombia-san-pedro-de-majagua-day-trip/) is a separate optional excursion involving a boat crossing. It should not be treated as an automatically included island day in the standard eight-day trip.

## What is included and what costs extra

The standard itinerary provides 2 nights in Bogotá, 2 in Medellín and 3 in Cartagena, transfers, excursions with an English-speaking guide and breakfasts according to the programme. Comuna 13 also has a local guide. International and domestic flights are excluded from the price.

Additional expenses include meals not listed as included, climbing Piedra del Peñol, the boat trip in Guatapé and a sea excursion on the free day. None is a compulsory part of the itinerary. Before buying, compare the main programme and your chosen optional activities against flight schedules.

If nature and the colourful river appeal to you, consider the [12-day Caño Cristales tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-beyond/). Travellers who want to see a coffee farm and spend several nights on an island should compare the [10-day VIP programme with Barú](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/). Explore further options in our [Colombia tours catalogue](/colombia/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the three-city tour

### Can I see all three cities in 8 days?

Yes. The programme includes 2 nights in Bogotá, 2 in Medellín and 3 in Cartagena. However, two domestic flights and the day in Guatapé make it a fairly busy journey.

### Is climbing Piedra del Peñol compulsory?

No. The staircase climb is an optional paid activity. Visiting Guatapé itself is included in the itinerary.

### Are the Rosario Islands included?

There is a free day in Cartagena. You can add the [San Pedro de Majagua excursion](/colombia/rosario-islands/colombia-san-pedro-de-majagua-day-trip/), but it is not a compulsory included visit.

### Will there be a Russian-speaking guide?

The confirmed standard programme provides an English-speaking guide and a local guide in Comuna 13. Russian-language guiding must be arranged separately.

lead: >-
  "Colombia Coffee" is a six-day journey through Bogotá and the coffee-growing region around Pereira. At its heart is a visit to a working coffee farm to explore how beans are grown, processed, roasted and tasted. The capital's historic attractions are complemented by an excursion to the Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá, walks in Salento and a nature trail among the wax palms of the Cocora Valley.
---

## Colombia Coffee tour: following the bean from plantation to cup

The defining feature of this trip is **a dedicated excursion day at a coffee farm, where you can follow the stages of coffee production**. The tour lasts 6 days and 5 nights. The first 3 nights are spent in Bogotá and the next 2 in Pereira. This sequence gives you time to explore the capital's cultural landmarks before turning to coffee production and mountain landscapes.

The itinerary suits travellers curious about coffee's flavour and origins, interested in colonial towns and happy to devote a day to a nature excursion. It is a complete journey through Colombia, however, rather than a professional roasting course or a certified barista training programme.

## The coffee farm: what the visit actually includes

On day four, after flying to [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), you take a private excursion to a coffee farm. We arrange a visit to one of the region's farms or Hacienda Morelia, depending on availability. A particular estate therefore cannot be guaranteed in advance.

A local specialist explains planting, selective hand-picking, drying, processing, grinding and roasting the beans. You will see views of the plantations, and the visit ends with **a tasting and barista demonstration**. This connects the drink's flavour characteristics to the ways its beans are grown and processed.

The region's coffee tradition extends far beyond a single farm. Colombia's Coffee Cultural Landscape is a UNESCO World Heritage property, recognised for agriculture adapted to steep mountain slopes and the settlements associated with it. This does not mean that every farm visited by tourists necessarily lies within the boundaries of the UNESCO site.

## Salento and the Cocora Valley: why they deserve a separate day

Day five is devoted to the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) and [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/). The focus shifts from coffee production to nature and mountain settlements.

In Cocora Valley, the programme includes an ecological trail, an introduction to wax palms, a discussion of local traditions and the symbolic planting of a seedling. Salento follows, with colonial streets, craft workshops and a viewpoint. This is a separate nature-and-culture excursion lasting around 7 hours, not an extension of a café tasting.

Combining the farm with Cocora reveals both production and the region's natural environment, unlike a visit to the coffee estate alone. Comfortable, non-slip shoes will be more useful than city footwear, and rain is possible on the nature trail.

## What complements the coffee experience in Bogotá

The first 3 days are spent in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and its surroundings. The capital's itinerary includes La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero collection, Bolívar Square and a trip up Monserrate. There is a separate excursion to the Salt Cathedral in [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/).

Museum schedules matter: the Gold Museum is closed on Mondays, while Casa de la Moneda and Donación Botero list Tuesdays as closing days. If your trip falls on those weekdays, the order of visits needs adjusting. This is particularly important on a short six-day tour, where there is little spare time to reschedule an attraction.

## What to consider: flights, excursion languages and meals

| Question | Programme arrangements |
|---|---|
| Accommodation | 3 nights in Bogotá, 2 in Pereira |
| Domestic flight | Bogotá–Pereira, paid separately |
| Coffee farm | Private excursion |
| Lunches on excursions | Additional charge |

The Bogotá–Pereira flight is not included in the published programme price, nor are international flights. An optional lunch at the coffee farm costs $20 per person; lunch on the Cocora excursion day is separately priced at $30 per person.

When choosing the language of your guide, read the arrangements for individual days. The day-by-day descriptions specify Spanish-speaking guides or specialists for the Bogotá city tour, the coffee farm and Cocora, while the general list of included services separately mentions an English-speaking guide. Confirm the language arrangements before booking rather than assuming English is provided at every stage.

## When to choose a longer itinerary

On the ["Colombia Live" tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-live/), the coffee farm and Cocora Valley form part of a broader thirteen-day journey that also includes [Tayrona](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/) and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). If coffee production and the Andes' natural valleys are your main priorities, the six-day version saves time and reduces regional transfers.

Other journeys where coffee genuinely forms the theme can be found among our [coffee tours](/interests/coffee-tours/). A tasting in a city café does not, by itself, turn any sightseeing tour into a dedicated coffee journey.

## Frequently asked questions about Colombia Coffee

### Can we visit Hacienda Morelia specifically?

We arrange a visit to a coffee farm or Hacienda Morelia, depending on availability. The exact estate is confirmed before the trip.

### Can guests take part in making coffee?

The excursion includes demonstrations of production stages, a tasting and a barista demonstration. Individual hands-on roasting for every guest or professional instruction is not advertised.

### Can I spend all 6 days without domestic flights?

The current itinerary includes a Bogotá–Pereira flight, paid for separately. Travelling overland instead would require agreement on a different transport plan and extra journey time.

### Are meals included in the tour?

Accommodation and the main excursions are listed in the programme; breakfasts are connected with the hotel stays. Lunches at the coffee farm and on the Cocora day are listed as optional paid extras. Check the tour itinerary for the precise meal arrangements.

  This private 11-day Colombia tour combines Bogotá, Lake Guatavita, the coffee region, Cartagena, three nights on San Andrés Island, and Medellín with Guatapé. Here is how the journey is organised, what is actually included, how it differs from the shorter programme, and how to interpret the accommodation options and prices.

## The many faces of Colombia in 11 days: from the Andes and coffee to the Caribbean

Our itinerary is designed for travellers who want to experience several very different parts of Colombia in one journey. It begins in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), continues through the coffee region around Pereira and Cocora Valley, then reaches the Caribbean coast in [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and on [San Andrés](/colombia/place/san-andres/) Island. The final section explores [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) and Guatapé.

The tour lasts 11 days and 10 nights. It is a private trip, with English-language guiding included under the published rate. Other guiding languages are arranged when booking. A key distinguishing feature is two full free days on San Andrés, staying at an all-inclusive resort.

## The first days: the capital, El Dorado and an underground cathedral

On the first day, a private guide meets you after arrival in Bogotá. The itinerary then explores La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero collection and the historic centre; a trip up Monserrate gives you a view of the city from above.

Day two takes you beyond the capital. First come Lake Guatavita and Guatavita town, associated with the El Dorado legend. Then you visit the Salt Cathedral in Zipaquirá, an underground complex in former mine workings where architecture meets the history of salt extraction. Lunch on this day is paid for separately.

Together, these two days introduce the country's history and culture. Travellers encounter pre-colonial stories, Spanish heritage and a modern metropolis.

## Pereira, Cocora Valley and coffee at El Ocaso farm

On day three, the programme moves into the coffee region. A walk with an eco-guide among the tall wax palms of [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) is planned. In Salento, you can see colourful streets and workshops, while a visit to [El Ocaso coffee farm](/colombia/place/el-ocaso-coffee-farm/) introduces the growing, harvesting, drying, processing and roasting of coffee beans.

This is a dedicated coffee experience that includes learning about production and tasting the result. For someone whose previous experience of Colombian coffee was only in a cup, a day in the coffee region often becomes a highlight of the journey.

Day four is set aside for more active pursuits: ziplining and horse riding. The programme can be adapted to a gentler pace, but any specific replacement must be agreed when booking.

## Cartagena and three nights on San Andrés

Day five includes a flight to Cartagena and an introduction to the fortified city: San Felipe de Barajas, the Clock Tower, historic squares, city walls and the architecture of the old centre.

On day six, travellers leave for San Andrés. Three nights are planned at an island resort, while days seven and eight are for relaxing beside the Caribbean with no compulsory sightseeing. You can enjoy the beach and the resort's services in accordance with its rate. Additional activities are arranged separately and charged on top of the programme.

This arrangement suits travellers who want a genuine break after several busy sightseeing days, rather than another daily sequence of transfers.

## Medellín, Comuna 13 and Guatapé

Day nine involves a flight to Medellín and a city tour. Stops include Botero Square, the Museum of Antioquia, the Palace of Culture, Comuna 13 and its street art, and El Castillo Museum.

The following day, travellers visit [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), known for its brightly painted facades and decorative reliefs on houses. Nearby is the granite El Peñón de Guatapé rock, with views over the reservoir. Day eleven ends with a transfer to Medellín airport.

Medellín is a substantial final section of the itinerary, not simply an overnight stop between domestic flights.

## Prices, accommodation and included services

The starting price is **from $4456 per person** for triple occupancy in 4★ hotels. Double occupancy in 4★ hotels costs $4523 per person and single occupancy costs $8622. In the 5★ category, prices are $4776 for TRP, $5282 for DBL and $9637 for SGL.

| Category and occupancy | Price per person |
|---|---:|
| 4★, triple | $4456 |
| 4★, double | $4523 |
| 5★, double | $5282 |

The price includes accommodation, breakfasts, private transfers, excursions according to the programme with English-speaking guides, and all-inclusive service during the specified nights on San Andrés. **Domestic flights along the itinerary and international air tickets are paid for separately.** Optional excursions, tips and personal expenses are also excluded.

Accommodation must be clarified before payment: the day-by-day itinerary shows one night in Cartagena and 10 nights in total, while the hotel table lists two nights in Cartagena and a total of 11 nights. The final accommodation calendar and calculation must be agreed without independently altering the stated rates.

## Who should choose the 11-day itinerary

This option appeals to travellers seeking a combination of culture, nature, coffee and several days of beach relaxation. If you would prefer to spend more time in cities and the coffee region without three nights on San Andrés, compare it with the [nine-day Colombia programme](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/), which finishes in Cartagena and includes the Rosario Islands.

The journey covers several distant regions; it helps to consider the number of flights and the pace of excursions in advance. Exact travel dates in 2027 are agreed when booking.

## Frequently asked questions about the tour

### How long does the journey last?

11 days. The programme states 10 nights, but the day-by-day plan and the Cartagena accommodation table differ. This needs clarification before payment.

### Are flights between cities included?

No. Domestic and international flights are excluded from the price.

### How many nights are spent on San Andrés?

The programme includes three nights and two full free days on the island. Accommodation is on an all-inclusive basis.

### Is a Russian-speaking guide provided?

The rate covers English-speaking guides. Guiding in another language must be agreed separately.

### What does the price from $4456 mean?

It is the per-person rate for triple occupancy in the 4★ hotel category, according to the price table.

lead: >-

Bogotá's museums, Lake Guatavita and the Salt Cathedral give way to Cartagena's colonial neighbourhoods and the Rosario Islands. ---

## Colombia in 5 days: connecting the Andes with the Caribbean

This itinerary is built around the contrast between [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) in the Andes and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) on the Caribbean coast. The first 2 nights are spent in the capital and the following 2 in Cartagena. During that time, travellers discover the country's colonial and pre-Columbian history, an underground religious complex and islands off the coast.

**Five days means a fairly packed programme here.** Your arrival day includes an introduction to Bogotá's historic centre; the next day is devoted to an excursion to Guatavita and Zipaquirá. On day 3, the group flies to Cartagena and explores the city. The Rosario Islands are scheduled for day 4, followed by an airport transfer on day 5. This sequence is too busy for a relaxed beach holiday with several days free to rest.

If you would like to add Medellín and Guatapé to Bogotá and Cartagena, compare the [7-day itinerary through three cities](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/). The five-day version is more convenient when time is limited and you want to finish your trip by the sea.

## Bogotá: museums, Monserrate and the Guatavita legend

In Bogotá, the itinerary begins in the historic La Candelaria district, the Gold Museum, the Mint, the Botero collection and Bolívar Square. Going up Monserrate offers a view of the city surrounded by mountains. This is a busy day, so the arrival time of your international flight is particularly important: it determines whether all the planned sightseeing can take place on the day you land.

Day two includes a trip to [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/), associated with the history and legends of Muisca rituals. The route then passes through [Guatavita town](/colombia/place/guatavita-town/) to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral. This is a full-day excursion outside the capital. Lunch at a local restaurant costs extra.

Bogotá sits high in the Andes, whereas Cartagena is at sea level. Temperatures, humidity and walking conditions change during the same journey. Bring clothes suitable for cooler weather in the capital, and lightweight clothing and sun protection for the coast.

## Cartagena and the Rosario Islands: how much time is spent by the sea

After flying from Bogotá, the group takes a sightseeing tour of [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). Colonial streets, historic squares and fortifications reflect the city's role in Caribbean trade. Its port, forts and monuments form part of a UNESCO World Heritage property.

The following day is dedicated to the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/). The programme includes a shared speedboat trip to San Pedro de Majagua on [Isla Grande](/colombia/place/isla-grande/), time to swim and relax, and a return to Cartagena. This day's price covers the marine fee, a Caribbean lunch, dessert, and coffee or tea. A private boat can be booked for an additional fee.

**The shared boat and private transfer are different elements of the service.** Private ground transport takes you to the pier, but the crossing to the island is shared with other participants. If a fully private journey on the water is essential to you, a paid alternative must be arranged separately.

The island excursion is the main opportunity for seaside relaxation on this five-day trip. There is no overnight stay on the islands: the group returns to its hotel in Cartagena.

## What is included and what you will pay for separately

The tour includes 4 hotel nights, 2 in Bogotá and 2 in Cartagena, daily breakfasts, excursions with an **English-speaking guide** and private transfers according to the itinerary. The island day includes a shared speedboat, lunch, dessert, coffee or tea and the marine fee.

**Air tickets are not included in the service price.** Remember to budget for the domestic Bogotá–Cartagena flight. International flights are paid for separately as well. Other extra costs include optional excursions, lunches outside the specified island day, dinners, selected drinks, tips and personal expenses.

The rates offer 4★ and 5★ hotels and SGL, DBL and TRP occupancy options. The starting amount of **$1863** applies to TRP occupancy in 4★ hotels, while DBL in the same category is listed at **$1883**. These figures cannot be compared without considering the number of occupants and the hotel category. The full rate schedule is available in the tour programme.

| Question before choosing | What to check |
|---|---|
| Intercity transport | Bogotá–Cartagena ticket is paid for separately |
| Guiding | Standard rate includes an English-speaking guide |
| Sea excursion | Shared boat included, private boat costs extra |
| Accommodation | 2 nights in Bogotá and 2 in Cartagena |

## Who is the 5-day itinerary for?

This tour is for travellers wanting a first impression of Colombia in a short time: the capital's history and museums, the Guatavita legend, the Salt Cathedral, Cartagena and a day on the islands. The itinerary combines cultural experiences with time by the sea.

It is less suitable for those who want several days without excursions or early departures, or who wish to explore Medellín. They should compare the [seven-day version with Medellín](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/) or other [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/). For a different balance between sightseeing and the coast, browse [cultural and historical journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/) and [beach holidays](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/colombia/).

## Frequently asked questions about the five-day Colombia trip

### Is the Bogotá–Cartagena flight included?

No. The domestic flight is paid for separately, as are international flights. Ground transfers on the published itinerary are included.

### Can I stay overnight on the Rosario Islands?

The five-day trip described here visits the islands during the day and returns to the hotel in Cartagena. An additional overnight stay on Isla Grande is not included.

### What language does the guide speak?

The standard rates include an **English-speaking guide**. Guiding in another language is discussed separately at booking.

### Are 5 days enough to see all of Colombia?

This is a brief introduction to two cities and their surroundings. Medellín, Guatapé, the Amazon and other regions are not part of the main itinerary.

  Ada Tours' nine-day itinerary visits Bogotá, Pereira, Medellín and Cartagena, with two nights in each city. Highlights include Lake Guatavita, Cocora Valley, El Ocaso coffee farm, Comuna 13, Guatapé and a day on the Rosario Islands. We explain the order of the journey, prices, flights and differences from the 11-day tour.
---

## Colombia in 9 days: Bogotá, the coffee region, Medellín and the Caribbean

The "Colombia in Four Chapters" tour links four destinations within one country. The first two days focus on [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and its surroundings. Next come Pereira, with its coffee plantations and the palms of Cocora Valley; [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), with its street art and nearby Guatapé; and finally [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), with its fortified historic centre and an excursion to the Rosario Islands.

The programme lasts **9 days and 8 nights**, with two nights in each of the four cities. It is a convenient option for a first extended trip if you want to discover Colombian history, nature and coffee culture without adding several more days at a separate island resort.

## Bogotá: La Candelaria and traces of the El Dorado legend

After arrival at El Dorado Airport, a private guide meets you. The Bogotá city tour includes La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero collection, the central square and Monserrate mountain.

On day two, the journey continues to Lake Guatavita, historic Guatavita town and the Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá. The ancient El Dorado legend is associated with rituals around the lake, while the underground cathedral reveals a very different aspect of the region's history: mining and religious architecture.

This sequence allows you to see both the capital and important sites nearby in two days. But the sightseeing schedule is demanding: Guatavita and Zipaquirá make for a full excursion beyond the city.

## Coffee country: Cocora, Salento and El Ocaso

On day three, a flight to Pereira begins the coffee-growing portion of the journey. Travellers walk among tall wax palms in [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/), then visit the town of Salento and [El Ocaso farm](/colombia/place/el-ocaso-coffee-farm/).

The coffee experience goes beyond tasting. At the farm, you learn about growing, processing, drying and roasting the beans. You will meet a local specialist and sample coffee in the region where it is produced.

Day four is devoted to ziplining and a horse ride. As in the longer programme, the day's activities can be adjusted for travellers who prefer less physical exertion; any substitutions are agreed separately.

## Medellín: street art and El Peñón rock

Day five involves travel to Medellín and a city tour. Stops include Botero Square, cultural landmarks, Comuna 13 with its stairways, murals and transformed urban environment, as well as El Castillo Museum.

The following day takes you to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). The town's streets are lined with colourful facades and raised decorative panels called zócalos. Nearby rises El Peñón de Guatapé, a rock famous for panoramic views of the reservoir.

Travellers should allow for climbs and staircases at certain viewpoints. Climbing to the top of the rock is not obligatory for every traveller, regardless of fitness.

## Cartagena and a day at sea on the Rosario Islands

The final two nights are spent in Cartagena. In the city, the itinerary includes San Felipe de Barajas Fortress and historic streets behind the defensive walls. Colonial buildings with wooden balconies, courtyards and squares present a very different urban landscape after the Andes.

Day eight is reserved for a sea excursion to the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) and relaxation around San Pedro de Majagua on Isla Grande. The format depends on the relevant excursion programme and sea conditions. The focus is on island nature and a single day beside the Caribbean, rather than a multi-day beach resort.

Day nine ends with departure from Cartagena.

## Prices and accommodation: understanding the categories

The starting price is **from $4041 per person**, based on triple occupancy in 4★ hotels. In the 4★ category, double occupancy costs $4058 per person and single occupancy $7830. For 5★ hotels, the rates are $4399 for TRP, $4836 for DBL and $8913 for SGL.

| Accommodation | Price per person |
|---|---:|
| 4★, triple | $4041 |
| 4★, double | $4058 |
| 5★, double | $4836 |

The programme includes two nights each in Bogotá, Pereira, Medellín and Cartagena, the stated excursions and transfers, specified meals and guiding. Rates are based on English-speaking guides; the language can be agreed separately. **International and domestic flights are paid for separately.** Exact travel dates within 2027 are agreed when arranging the trip.

## Nine or eleven days: which itinerary should you choose?

| 9 days | 11 days |
|---|---|
| Four cities | San Andrés is added |
| One day on the Rosario Islands | Three nights on San Andrés |
| Greater emphasis on excursions | Two free days at the beach |

The [11-day "Many Faces of Colombia" programme](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) retains the cultural and coffee experiences but adds a separate island stay and distributes the final days differently. The nine-day tour ends on the Caribbean coast in Cartagena.

Both journeys are busy and involve several domestic transfers. For a more relaxed experience, discuss adding nights or reducing the sightseeing schedule.

## Frequently asked questions about the tour

### How many nights are spent in each city?

Two nights each in Bogotá, Pereira, Medellín and Cartagena, making eight in total.

### Does the programme include San Andrés?

No. The nine-day itinerary includes a day on the Rosario Islands; San Andrés is part of the 11-day version.

### What is included in the coffee programme?

Cocora Valley, Salento and a visit to El Ocaso farm to learn about coffee production and taste it.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. They are paid for separately from the quoted tour price.

### How much does the trip cost?

From $4041 per person, based on triple occupancy in 4★ hotels according to the price table.
